newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korean won closes lower despite BOK dlr selling.
newsitem.headline: S.Korean won closes lower despite BOK dlr selling.

text.p: A strong demand for the dollar sent the won to a lower close on Monday despite the central bank's repeated dollar-selling intervention, dealers said.

Dealers said the Bank of Korea jumped into the interbank market in early afternoon trading at around 855.00 won to the U.S. unit and later at around 856.00 won shortly before the close. The bank denied intervening, as it routinely does.
The won closed at 855.80 to the U.S. unit, after opening the day at 854.60. It moved in a 854.50-856.00 range.
"The 856 won level now appears meaningless after the 855 resistance was broken easily," said a local bank dealer.
Dealers said economic fundamentals showed a room for the won to go down further.
The dollar has gained by more than 10 won so far this year. "But fundamentals show there is no reason why the U.S. unit should not rise further," said a foreign bank dealer.
Dealers said the won was pressured by the nation's huge trade deficit and a gloomy outlook for this year's exports.
They said they expected the won's base mid-rate to be pegged at 855.00 on Tuesday, compared with Monday's 854.10.
